role: Southeast Asia's most established packaging and testing cluster

strengths.text: Decades-deep packaging and test cluster in Penang and Kulim (Intel, Infineon, AMD, Micron, ASE, AT&S), with about 13% of global assembly, packaging and test activity (a share of activity, not capacity).
Infineon's Kulim site is the world's largest 200mm silicon-carbide power fab (Phase 1 opened August 2024).
Broad electronics base plus a large data-center build-out in Johor, next to Singapore.

constraints.text: Advanced packaging is still early: the national target is about 7% of global advanced packaging by 2035.
Shortage of senior engineers, with talent drawn to Singapore.

watch.text: Whether the national talent target (60,000 by 2030) turns into experienced engineers.
Firm power for a large site, which has to be confirmed with the utility (TNB).

role: Fast-growing electronics and back-end base, with rising chip design

strengths.text: Large foreign-invested electronics manufacturing base, led by Samsung and its suppliers.
Established back-end sites: Amkor's US$1.6B campus in Bac Ninh (opened 2023) and a large Intel assembly and test site in Ho Chi Minh City.
Chip design is rising fastest in the group: about 7,000 designers (reported), with Marvell and Faraday R&D.

constraints.text: Little front-end supply chain; back-end equipment and materials arrive mainly through foreign investors.
43% of firms reported power outages in 2024.

watch.text: Whether the talent target (about 50,000 by 2030) turns into deployable engineers; today's reported stock is about 15,000.
Dry-season hydropower shortfalls and peak curtailment, a risk for plants that run 24/7.

role: Automotive, power-electronics and electronics manufacturing base

strengths.text: The clearest demand for mature-node and power chips, from automotive and power electronics.
Established back-end and power-component manufacturing (Infineon), plus a hard-disk-drive and circuit-board base.
A government five-year semiconductor plan and investment incentives in the Eastern Economic Corridor.

constraints.text: Front-end talent and supply chain are still being built.
The shift to electric vehicles is reshaping the automotive base, so demand is still moving.

watch.text: How Infineon's new back-end plant in Samut Prakan ramps up (first building ready early 2026).
Progress toward about 80,000 semiconductor workers under the five-year plan (a target, not today's workforce).

role: Early-stage, policy-driven market with long-term ambitions

strengths.text: Large domestic market, with electric-vehicle and local-content electronics demand emerging.
Arm and Danantara agreed to train up to about 15,000 people in chip design, with a first cohort of about 1,000 from May 2026.
Some back-end activity in Batam (Infineon), though still thin.

constraints.text: The thinnest ecosystem and supply chain of the five (author comparison).
Power supply outside Java and Bali is weak and uneven.

watch.text: Whether the Arm program grows into a real design industry; it is a talent program, not a manufacturing commitment.
The 2025–2035 silica-downstreaming roadmap, which is a plan rather than capacity.

role: Veteran packaging and testing base with an English-speaking workforce

strengths.text: Long-established assembly, test and packaging base; the world's 9th-largest chip exporter (OECD).
Electronics make up about 60% of exports.
About 47,000 engineering and technology graduates in 2021/22.

constraints.text: Among the region's highest electricity prices, about US$0.15–0.20 per kWh.
43.9% of firms reported power outages in 2023.
Chip design is thin: about 13 firms and 1,000 designers.

watch.text: Grid reliability outside Metro Manila, where many plants keep their own generators.
Progress on the 128,000-person upskilling target, which measures something different from graduates.
